endpoint_circuit_open.title: Endpoint circuit opened
endpoint_circuit_open.body: {platform} {endpoint} tripped: {risk_rate}% of the last {samples} requests hit risk control. It will be probed again in {retry_after} seconds.

pool_empty.title: Identity pool empty
pool_empty.body: No active identity is left for {platform}. Requests are queued or rejected until the pool recovers.

pool_below_min.title: Identity pool below its low-water mark
pool_below_min.body: {platform} has {active} active identities, below the configured minimum of {minimum}.

proxy_unhealthy.title: Proxy unreachable
proxy_unhealthy.body: Proxy {proxy} failed {failures} consecutive probes and was taken out of rotation.

signature_stale.title: Signing algorithm may be stale
signature_stale.body: Local signing disagreed with the browser for {platform} {endpoint} on {parameters}. That platform is signed by browser-rpc until the native algorithm is re-ported.

cookie_expiring.title: Session cookie expiring
cookie_expiring.body: Identity {identity_id} expires in {days} days. Re-import it to keep the logged-in pool intact.

backup_failed.title: Backup failed
backup_failed.body: The scheduled backup did not complete: {reason}.

notify.footer: Sent by your dtk instance. Alert channels are configured in the console.

test.title: Test alert
test.body: This is a test alert from your dtk instance, sent to the {channel} channel because someone asked for it in the console. Nothing is wrong and no action is needed.

capacity_warning.title: Disk filling up
capacity_warning.body: {detail}. Background collection is still running; it will pause automatically at {hard_stop}%.

capacity_paused.title: Background collection paused
capacity_paused.body: {detail}. New download jobs and scheduled collection have stopped so the instance keeps serving reads. Nothing has been deleted; free space or raise capacity.hard_stop_percent to resume.

media_evicted.title: Stored media cleaned up
media_evicted.body: {files} downloads ({freed}) were removed to stay under the {ceiling} media ceiling. Pinned downloads were not touched, and every record is still in the library - only the files are gone.

sched.max_wait_seconds: How long a request waits for a free identity before it degrades into a background task.
sched.queue_max: Maximum requests allowed to queue for an identity. Beyond this the API rejects immediately with Retry-After.
sched.cooldown_base_seconds: How long an identity rests after its first risk-control hit. Each consecutive hit doubles it.
sched.cooldown_max_seconds: Cooldown ceiling. An identity that reaches it is marked degraded instead of cooling again.
sched.circuit_risk_threshold: Risk-control rate above which an endpoint is tripped, between 0 and 1.
sched.circuit_min_samples: Minimum requests observed before an endpoint may trip, so a short burst of failures cannot open the circuit.
sched.circuit_min_identities: How many distinct identities must be failing before an endpoint trips. This separates a broken endpoint from a single broken identity.

pool.target_size: How many identities the pool tries to keep per platform.
pool.min_size: Low-water mark per platform. Dropping below it raises an alert and triggers minting.
pool.health_prior: Assumed success rate for an identity with no history yet, between 0 and 1. It decides how eagerly a freshly minted identity is scheduled.
pool.max_fail_streak: Consecutive failures after which an identity stops counting towards the pool level, so the filler mints a replacement instead of counting a session that serves nothing. The failure streak is used rather than the health score because the score is empty until there is traffic, and scoring a freshly minted identity as unusable would turn the low-water mark into a minting loop.

signing.mode: Which signer produces the request signature: the browser, the in-process algorithms, or automatic switching between them.
signing.fallback_enabled: Whether the signer this mode does not prefer may still be used when the preferred one is unavailable. Turning it off is how you find out which signer is actually carrying the traffic.
signing.rpc_timeout_seconds: Ceiling for a single browser-rpc signing call.

cache.content_ttl: How long a parsed video detail stays reusable before it is fetched again.
cache.author_ttl: How long a parsed user profile stays reusable.
cache.list_ttl: How long a parsed list page stays reusable. Lists change more often than a single item, so this is usually the shortest of the three.

snapshot.min_interval_seconds: Deduplication window for the content history. A second snapshot of the same item inside this window is skipped rather than stored.

retention.request_log_days: How long per-request log rows are kept before they are dropped. Content snapshots are never deleted automatically.
retention.identity_events_days: How long identity state changes are kept. Long enough to explain why an identity was retired.
retention.task_days: How long finished task rows are kept.
retention.task_result_hours: How long a task's result payload is kept. Shorter than the task row itself, because the payload is the bulky part.
retention.retired_identity_days: How long a retired identity's row is kept after it is retired. The cookies are already wiped at retirement; this is only the record of the identity having existed, and without a window the table grows by one row for every identity the pool ever loses.

api.default_language: Language used when a request specifies none. A request may always override it with ?lang= or an Accept-Language header.
api.default_rate_limit_per_min: Requests per minute allowed for one API key. Abuse protection, not billing.
api.max_wait_seconds: Largest value a caller may pass to ?wait=. It bounds how long one request can hold a connection open.
api.mcp_tool_timeout: How long one MCP tool call may run before it is cancelled.

security.url_allowlist: Extra hostnames a short link may redirect through. The built-in platform list always applies; each entry is matched as a whole hostname, belongs to no platform, and widens the SSRF surface, so add one only to rescue a redirect chain that dies on an unlisted hop.
security.cors_allow_origins: Browser origins allowed to call this API. Empty means same-origin only. '*' would hand your API keys to any site the user visits.
security.cors_allow_credentials: Whether cross-origin requests may carry cookies. Only meaningful with an explicit origin list; it cannot be combined with '*'.
security.enable_task_webhook: Whether a task may call back to a caller-supplied URL. That URL is an SSRF vector, so this is off by default.

notify.enabled: Master switch for outgoing alerts. Off means alerts are still recorded but nothing is sent.
notify.channels: Where alerts are delivered: a list of channel descriptors, each with a type, a url and a language.
notify.language: Language for alert text, for channels that do not specify their own.

system.check_updates: Whether this instance may contact the project to check for a newer release. It makes an outbound request, so it is opt-in.

description.security.request_proxy: Whether a caller may pass ?proxy= to route their request through their own egress. 'deny' refuses the parameter, 'public' allows only publicly routable addresses, and 'any' also allows loopback and private ranges - which lets anyone holding an API key reach this server's own network.
description.api.public_endpoints: Endpoints this instance serves without an API key, each written as '<METHOD> <path>' exactly as the API document shows it, for example 'GET /api/v1/{platform}/video'. Empty means everything needs a credential, which is the default. Admin, authentication and setup endpoints can never be opened, whatever is listed here.
description.archive.enabled: Keep parsed posts and authors in the database after the task result expires. With this off the instance keeps only its logs and metric history, and a post you parsed today cannot be looked up tomorrow.
description.archive.store_raw: Also keep each platform's untouched payload alongside the normalized record, so a new field can be back-computed later without re-crawling. Off by default: the parsers produce one for every object, making it the largest single thing this instance can choose to store.
description.retention.content_days: Delete archived posts last seen more than this many days ago. 0 means never delete, which is the default - the archive exists precisely to outlive the platform. Disk is protected by the capacity guard instead.
description.capacity.warn_percent: Disk usage percent at which this instance raises a warning. Measured on the filesystem, so it accounts for WAL, indexes and anything else sharing the volume.
description.capacity.hard_stop_percent: Disk usage percent at which background collection and new download jobs stand down. Interactive API reads are never paused, and nothing is ever deleted - a full disk should degrade the instance, not take it offline or destroy what it has collected.

media.enabled: Allow media downloads. Turning it off refuses new jobs and leaves stored files alone; nothing is deleted by this switch.
media.max_bytes: How much disk stored media may occupy. Past it the oldest unpinned downloads are removed until the volume is back under, and an alert says what went. Pinned downloads are never removed. 0 disables cleanup entirely.
media.max_file_bytes: Ceiling for one file, counted on bytes actually written rather than on the size the server claims. A transfer that reaches it is refused and leaves nothing behind.
media.mirror_max_age_seconds: How old an archived media link may be before a download re-parses the post to get fresh ones. Signed CDN links expire within hours; 0 always re-parses, which costs one request from the identity pool.

watchlist.enabled: Run scheduled collection. Turning it off leaves the entries and everything they have collected alone; it simply stops submitting runs.
watchlist.min_interval_seconds: Shortest interval any watched target may be given. A target collected every few seconds does not produce a better time series - it spends the whole identity pool on one author and starves everything else.
watchlist.default_interval_seconds: Interval a newly watched target gets when none is specified.
watchlist.batch_size: How many due entries one tick may queue. The rest stay due and go on the next tick, so a large watchlist is spread over minutes rather than landing all at once in front of whoever is using the API.

description.archive.recheck_after_days: How old a post's last existence check may be before it is checked again. This is what makes "which of the things I saved are gone" answerable at all - without it, a post deleted the day after it was archived stays marked live forever. 0 turns rechecking off.
description.archive.recheck_batch: How many posts one recheck pass verifies. Each is a real request through the identity pool, so this is the knob that decides what the answer costs.
description.archive.recheck_pause_seconds: Seconds between the individual requests a recheck or backfill makes. The scheduler paces requests per identity, which does nothing about a platform limit that counts requests per address - measured: 20 requests in 13 seconds were all rejected, while one a minute later succeeded. Nobody is waiting on these passes, so slow costs nothing.
description.security.webhook_secret: Shared secret used to sign task callbacks, sent as X-Dtk-Signature: sha256=<hmac of the exact body>. Without it a receiver has no way to tell a real notification from anyone who guessed the callback URL. Leave empty to send callbacks unsigned.

openapi.description: Self-hosted data API for Douyin and TikTok. Submit a link, get normalized content back. Errors carry a stable code plus a message in the requested language; append ?lang=zh for Chinese.

tag.admin: Instance administration; requires the admin scope.
tag.archive: What this instance has already collected. Answered from local storage.
tag.auth: Signing in, sessions, and the account you are signed in as.
tag.content: Platform-agnostic reads: hand any of these a link or an id.
tag.downloads: Media this instance has stored on its own disk. A sink, never a relay: bytes are never streamed back to a caller.
tag.ios: The iOS Shortcut this instance serves, ready to install.
tag.setup: First-run: the only endpoints that answer before an administrator exists.
tag.tasks: Asynchronous task submission, polling and events.
tag.tools: Building blocks: link parsing, signing and guest identity minting.

api_keys_create.description: Mint a key and show it once.

api_keys_list.description: Every API key on this instance, newest first.

archive_backfill.description: Walks one author's posts past the first page and archives every one. Separate from the watchlist on purpose: a watchlist entry is for what is new and runs forever, while a backfill is a one-off with a very different cost. Stops at the first empty page, at the page ceiling, or when the platform says there is no more history.

archive_delete.description: The one call in the archive that destroys something. Not reversible and there is no trash: the record goes, its collection memberships go with it, and unless `media` is false the stored files are removed from disk as well. `media` defaults to true because that is what "delete this" means about a video the instance is holding. Files are removed before rows, so the worst case is bytes with no record rather than a record offering a download it cannot deliver.

archive_export.description: Stream every matching post as newline-delimited JSON, a page at a time rather than buffered, so the size of your own collection is not what breaks the export. Requires the archive:export scope, which ordinary read keys do not carry.

archive_get.description: One post as this instance last saw it, media manifest included. The signed CDN links inside it expire; the web URL is the part that survives.

archive_list.description: One page of what this instance has already collected, newest sighting first. Answers from local storage - no identity is spent, nothing is fetched, and a post that has since been deleted is still here with its availability saying so. Filters combine; paging is by cursor.

archive_recheck.description: Verifies that archived posts are still on the platform. A deleted post answers not-found, which is the finding rather than a failure: the record is kept and marked deleted, so it stays searchable and exportable with the truth attached. Each post is one real request through the identity pool, so the batch is bounded and the pass runs in the background.

archive_stats.description: How many posts and authors this instance holds, with a per-platform breakdown.

auth_login.summary: Exchange a password for a session cookie
auth_login.description: Sign in to the console and receive a session cookie.

auth_logout.description: Idempotent on purpose: logging out twice is not an error.

auth_me.description: Who the current credential belongs to.

auth_password.description: Requires the current password even inside an authenticated session.

auth_session_revoke.description: ``session_ref`` is the digest from the list, never the token itself.

auth_sessions.description: Every device currently signed in as you.

author_followers.description: One page of the accounts that follow an author. TikTok only: Douyin serves its follow graph only to a signed-in identity, so asking for it there returns an error naming the platforms that do support it.

author_following.description: One page of the accounts an author follows. TikTok only, and accounts hide this side of the graph far more often than their followers, so an empty page is a common and correct answer.

author_likes.description: One page of the posts an author has publicly liked. TikTok answers a guest request, and an empty page usually means the author keeps their likes private. Douyin does not serve this list to a guest identity at all and needs an imported logged-in one.

author_posts.description: One page of an author's own posts, newest first, in the same shape as the single post endpoint. Page through with cursor.

author_profile.description: One author's public profile: nickname, signature, avatar, verification state and follower, following, like and post counts.

backup_list.description: Archives the server can see, newest first.

backup_restore.description: Queue a restore of one archive.

batch.description: Submits many links in one call and returns a task id per link. Each link is scheduled independently, so one failure does not hold up the rest.

collections_add.description: Adding a post that is already in the collection is a no-op rather than an error: the console sends whatever is selected, and part of a selection is routinely already there. A post that is not in the archive is skipped, so one stale card does not refuse the other nineteen. Returns how many were newly added.

collections_create.description: Make a new named set, empty until posts are added to it. The name is unique case-insensitively and whitespace in it is collapsed. `note` is free text the console shows under the name and nothing ever parses.

collections_delete.description: Removes the collection itself. The posts stay in the archive and the files stay on disk: a collection is a label, and deleting a label is not deleting what it was on.

collections_list.description: Every collection, with how many posts is in each. A collection is the one grouping the library offers that is not derived from the posts: author, platform and collection date all come out of the record, and this one comes out of somebody deciding.

collections_remove.summary: Take posts out of a collection
collections_remove.description: Removes membership only; the posts stay in the archive. A POST rather than a DELETE because it carries a body, and a DELETE with a body is the kind of thing intermediaries drop.

collections_update.description: Change the name, the note, or both. Membership is untouched. Send `note` as null to clear it; leave it out of the body entirely to keep whatever is there - the two are different requests that would otherwise look identical.

comment_replies.description: One page of replies underneath a single comment. Pass comment_id together with the post, identified by either url or aweme_id.

comments.summary: Top level comments on a post
comments.description: One page of top level comments on a post, with author, like count and reply count. Page through with cursor; a response with no cursor is the last page.

content_detail.summary: One post, video or image album
content_detail.description: One post - a video or an image album - with its media URLs, caption, statistics and author. Identify it by either url or aweme_id.

diagnose.description: Queue the same diagnosis the setup wizard finishes with (doc 15).

downloads_cancel.description: Stops a transfer that has not finished. Nothing is deleted: files already complete stay where they are, and removing files is the cleanup sweep's job rather than a DELETE's.

downloads_create.description: Fetches one already-archived post's media onto this instance's own disk. Takes a content key rather than a URL: nothing a caller sends decides which host is dialled. Answers 202 with a download id; the files land on the operator's volume and are never served back through this API.

downloads_file.description: Serve one file this instance has already stored, to a browser. The path is rebuilt from the stored record - the download's own directory plus a name that has to appear in its file list - so the only thing a caller chooses is which record, never where on the disk to read. Nothing is fetched: files evicted to stay under the media ceiling answer 404, and asking for the download again is what restores them.

downloads_get.description: One download and every file in it: name, size, sha256 and content type, and whether the files are still stored.

downloads_list.description: What this instance has been asked to store, newest first, with each file's size and sha256. A row whose on_disk is false was collected and later removed to stay under the media ceiling - which, unlike never having fetched it, can be undone by asking again.

downloads_pin.description: Exempts one download from the size-based cleanup. This is the only way to keep a file the ceiling would otherwise remove, and a post the platform has since deleted cannot be fetched again.

downloads_storage.description: How much disk stored media occupies and how much it is allowed to, measured on the volume rather than summed from the database, plus whether the downloader container is reachable.

endpoints_access.summary: Which endpoints are served without a key
endpoints_access.description: Every endpoint, with whether it currently needs a credential.

endpoints_health.description: Every declared endpoint, whether or not it has traffic.

health.description: Reports database, cache, browser RPC and identity pool health. Safe to poll from an uptime monitor.

identities_import.description: Detect the paste format, report what was understood, then store it.

identities_list.summary: List identities with state and health

identities_mint.description: Queue a minting job per identity requested.

identities_pool.summary: Pool level against its low-water mark
identities_pool.description: What the background refill job compares, per platform. `usable` counts live identities whose consecutive failure streak is still under `pool.max_fail_streak` - not the row count, because an identity that fails every request stays live and would otherwise keep a dead pool looking full. Below `pool.min_size` the worker mints one identity per minute until the pool is back at `pool.target_size`. `can_mint` is false when this deployment has no browser container, in which case the marks have no effect and the pool is whatever was imported by hand.

identities_retire.description: Retire and wipe. The statistics stay, the credential does not (doc 05).

identities_test.description: Queue a single real request on this identity.

ios_shortcut.description: Version, download link and release notes for the companion iOS Shortcut, rendered in the requested language.

metrics_timeseries.summary: Request volume and outcomes over time
metrics_timeseries.description: Raw buckets. Series selection and zooming happen in the browser (doc 07).

mix_posts.summary: Posts inside a mix or playlist
mix_posts.description: One page of the posts collected in a mix - Douyin's series, TikTok's playlist. The id comes from any post that belongs to one: mix_info on Douyin, playlistId on TikTok.

notify_test.description: Prove the channel works before an incident depends on it.

parse.description: Detects the platform and content kind from the URL, then returns the normalized record. Add ?wait= to block for a result instead of polling the task.

proxies_create.description: Add one egress to the pool.

proxies_delete.summary: Delete a proxy and retire what used it
proxies_delete.description: Delete one egress, and retire every identity bound to it.

proxies_import.summary: Bulk import a pasted proxy list
proxies_import.description: Accept a block of lines and report the fate of each one.

proxies_test.description: Queue a connectivity and GeoIP probe for this egress.

proxies_update.description: Change one proxy's URL, label or geography.

settings_list.description: Every runtime setting, with its current value and where that came from.

settings_reset.summary: Reset one setting to its inherited value
settings_reset.description: Delete the override so the key falls back to the environment or default.

settings_update.description: Change one runtime setting; it takes effect without a restart.

setup_init.description: Consume the setup token and create the administrator.

setup_status.summary: Whether this instance has an administrator yet
setup_status.description: Unauthenticated by necessity: it is what the wizard asks first.

task_cancel.description: Gives up on a task that has not started. Only a queued task is stopped; one already running is left alone and reported as running, because its request is in flight and the identity's quota is already spent - recording a failure the worker never had would make the endpoint's risk rate lie. Nothing is deleted.

task_events.description: Server-sent events until the task settles or the deadline passes.

task_get.description: Returns the task state and, once it is done, its result. Results expire; re-submit if the task is gone.

tools_identity.summary: Mint a guest identity and return it
tools_identity.description: Drive a real browser to the platform and hand back the cookies it was issued - the half of the work no algorithm can produce. Takes tens of seconds, requires the identity:manage scope, and stores nothing: use the admin mint endpoint instead to add one to this instance's own pool.

tools_parse_batch.summary: Identify many links and ids at once
tools_parse_batch.description: `/tools/parse-url` answers one at a time, which is the wrong shape for what people actually have: a column pasted out of a spreadsheet, or the output of a scrape. Nothing here touches the network, so a thousand lines cost one request and no identity. Each line is tried as a link first and as a bare post id second; an id is checked against its own embedded timestamp, since both platforms mint ids whose high 32 bits are the Unix second they were issued. That check cannot tell a post that never existed from one since deleted - a plausible id is a plausible id - but it names a typo for free, instead of letting it become an upstream request that spends an identity to be told the same thing. Blank lines and duplicates are dropped.

tools_parse_url.description: Work out what a link points at without fetching anything: platform, resource kind and the id that names it. This is the id extraction v4 published as a dozen separate routes. Short links cannot be resolved without following them and come back needing expansion.

tools_sign.description: Compute the signature parameters a platform API URL needs. Pure arithmetic - nothing is fetched and no identity is spent. The User-Agent is hashed into the signature, so send the request with the same one the response echoes back; TikTok also checks that the TLS fingerprint agrees with it.

users_delete.description: Delete a console account and revoke its sessions.

users_update.summary: Change a role or reset a password
users_update.description: The password reset an administrator performs for someone else.

watchlist_create.description: Start collecting one author or post on a schedule.

watchlist_list.description: Every target this instance collects on a timer, soonest due first.

watchlist_pause.description: Stop all scheduled collection without losing the list.

watchlist_update.summary: Change or pause a watched target
watchlist_update.description: Change the interval, the page depth, or whether it runs at all.

param.aweme_id: The post id, as an alternative to url. Provide exactly one of the two.
param.comment_id: The parent comment whose replies you want. Ids come from the comments endpoint.
param.cursor: Opaque cursor from the previous page; omit for the first page.
param.identity: Send the request as this identity and no other, by id. For content only that account can see, such as your own private posts, fetched with a jar you imported from your own browser. Requires identity:manage; the request is never served from another identity and never from the response cache.
param.include_raw: Also return the platform's own untouched payload alongside the normalized record.
param.lang: Response language for human-readable text. One of en or zh; anything else falls back to en.
param.mix_id: The mix or playlist to read. Douyin returns it as mix_info, TikTok as playlistId.
param.platform: Which platform the request is addressed to: douyin or tiktok. It must match the link you pass.
param.proxy: Send the upstream request through this proxy, as a full URL such as http://host:port. Refused unless an administrator has enabled security.request_proxy.
param.q: Substring of the title or description. Matched as a substring rather than by word, so it behaves the same in Chinese as in English.
param.refresh: Ignore any cached or in-flight answer and make the request again. Two things make a repeat return the earlier answer - this instance joins an identical task that is already running or recently finished, and it caches the shaped body - and this turns off both. The fresh answer is still cached. It costs an identity and an upstream request, so it is for checking whether something changed rather than for every call. How long the cached answer lives depends on what was asked for and is set in the console: cache.content_ttl for one post (30 minutes by default), cache.author_ttl for a profile (15 minutes), cache.list_ttl for anything paged (5 minutes). Entries expire on their own and Redis is capped below its container limit, dropping the least recently used expiring keys before it fills, so the cache cannot grow without bound.
param.sec_user_id: The author's stable id, as an alternative to url. On TikTok this is secUid.
param.url: A link to the resource. Text with a link inside it is accepted, so clipboard content from the apps can be sent unedited.
param.wait: Seconds to wait for the task before returning 202 with a task id.

response.202: Accepted and queued. `data.task_id` names the task to poll.
response.400: The request was rejected. `error.code` says why.
response.401: No API key or session, or it is not valid.
response.403: Authenticated, but this credential lacks the scope.
response.404: No such resource, or the platform says the content is gone.
response.429: Rate limited. `error.retry_after` says when to come back.
response.500: An unhandled error. `meta.request_id` identifies it in the logs.
response.502: The platform refused, withheld the payload, or changed shape.
response.503: The identity pool, the queue or an upstream endpoint is unavailable.
response.error: The request failed. The code field is stable and machine-readable; the message field is localized.

security.api_key: Create one on the console's API keys page, then send it as this header. Bearer authorization works too.
security.session: Set by signing in to the console. A browser sends it automatically, which is why Try it out works here when you are signed in.

openapi.envelope: Every response has this shape, errors included. `data` carries the endpoint's own payload and is null whenever `success` is false; `error.code` is a stable identifier that is never translated, while `error.message` is rendered in the language you asked for.

reason.risk_across_identities: Risk control hit {risk_rate}% of the last {samples} requests, across {identities} identities

reason.components_browser_rpc_down: postgres and redis are reachable; browser-rpc is not ({detail})
reason.egress_unreachable: no platform domain could be reached directly
reason.proxies_no_session: no database session or cipher available to read the proxy list
reason.proxies_unreadable: the proxy list could not be read; see the component step
reason.proxies_all_failed: none of the {total} configured proxies answered
reason.pool_unreadable: the identity table could not be read; see the component step
reason.pool_below_minimum: {active} active identities, below the low-water mark of {minimum}
reason.signing_no_browser_rpc: browser-rpc is not configured, so there is no second signer to compare the native algorithm against
reason.signing_mismatch: native signing disagrees with the browser for {platforms}
reason.signing_not_comparable: cannot compare native and browser signing for {platforms}

action.components_unreachable: Check that the postgres and redis containers are running and that DTK_DATABASE_URL and DTK_REDIS_URL point at them.
action.components_browser_rpc_down: Minting and the signing fallback are unavailable. Start the browser container, or import cookies manually and stay on the native signer.
action.egress_unreachable: This machine has no usable route to the platforms. Check DNS, the host firewall, and whether outbound traffic needs a proxy.
action.egress_partial: Requests for the unreachable platform will depend entirely on a working proxy.
action.proxies_none: Every identity will share this machine's egress IP. That is fine for a first look and a correlation risk for a busy pool.
action.proxies_all_failed: Check the proxy credentials and whether the provider still allows this machine's IP. Identities bound to a dead proxy cannot recover.
action.proxies_partial: Retire or replace the proxies that failed; their identities will keep failing until you do.
action.pool_empty: Mint identities, or import a cookie jar. Until the pool has one usable identity every request is rejected or queued.
action.pool_below_minimum: Mint more identities, or lower pool.min_size if this is deliberate.
action.signing_no_browser_rpc: Configure DTK_BROWSER_RPC_URL to enable the shadow comparison that detects a stale signing algorithm before the risk rate does.
action.signing_mismatch: The native algorithm has drifted from the platform's. Those platforms now sign through browser-rpc; open an issue with this report so the algorithm can be updated.
action.smoke_failed: Read the failing step above first; a smoke failure is usually a symptom of the proxy, pool or signing step, not its own fault.
action.step_crashed: This is a bug in dtk. Please report it with this report attached.
action.signing_not_comparable: The browser reference implements a different version of the algorithm, so a structural comparison against it says nothing either way. The native path is unaffected and still serves requests; re-derive the invariants from the current bundle to restore the check.

warning.no_cookies: No cookies could be parsed from the pasted text.
warning.logged_in_session: This cookie set carries a logged-in session, which is as good as the account password. Use a dedicated account rather than your main one.
warning.unknown_browser: The browser could not be inferred from the User-Agent, so no TLS profile can be matched. Supply the exact User-Agent these cookies were copied from.
warning.no_useful_cookies: None of the optional cookies are present, so this identity will be weak. Any of {optional} would strengthen it.

body_limit.exceeded: The request body is larger than this instance accepts; the ceiling is {limit_kib} KiB.
